comments.body:
## /rebar-debug Stage 1 (Gather) — interim finding, recorded before the cause is confirmed

Posting now rather than at Phase 1 exit because it corrects a premise in this ticket's own
description, and that correction should survive an interrupted session.

### Correction: `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` is NOT a wall-clock guard

The description says the knob is "wired into both the Bedrock client
(`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:95` -> `read_timeout`/`connect_timeout`) and a wall-clock guard
(`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:376`)". Reading `structured_run.py:376` on origin/main, that
second site is not a wall-clock guard:

```python
if cfg.timeout_s:
    model_settings["timeout"] = float(cfg.timeout_s)
```

`model_settings["timeout"]` is a pydantic-ai `ModelSettings` field mapping to the underlying
**httpx request timeout** — the code comment at :370 says so explicitly ("`timeout` is a base
ModelSettings field mapping to the underlying httpx/Anthropic client request timeout"). The
Bedrock mapping is the same shape: botocore `read_timeout`/`connect_timeout`, i.e. per-socket-
phase bounds.

**So both wirings bound the MODEL HTTP CALL only. Nothing bounds the operation as a whole.**
The framing "the timeout was bypassed" is therefore wrong in a way that matters: the timeout was
never in scope for the region that hung. Every step after the model response — attestation
signing, snapshot materialization, sidecar/banking writes, store append, `git` commit, `git`
push — runs with no time bound at all.

This is consistent with, and predicted by, observation 4: pid 33196 at **87.7% CPU** at t+1h18m
and **0.0%** at t+3h03m. It finished compute inside the guarded region and then wedged in the
unguarded one.

### Supporting structural evidence: the unguarded region is large

An AST pass over `src/rebar` (every `subprocess.run` / `Popen` / `call` / `check_output` node,
checking for a `timeout` keyword) finds:

- **93** subprocess call sites total
- **61** with **no `timeout=`**
- **54** of those also do not set `stdin`/`input`, so they inherit the parent's stdin and can
  block on a prompt (credentials, an ssh passphrase, a host-key confirmation)

Concentrated on exactly the post-LLM paths: every `git` call in `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`
(573, 591, 607), `llm/workflow/snapshot.py` (83, and a `Popen` at 181), `_store/push.py:209`,
`llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:515`, `llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:380`,
`llm/code_review/finalize.py:94`, `_commands/txn.py:154`, `_commands/close_precheck.py:328`,
`attest/sshsig.py` (49, 80, 142), `_opcert_signing.py` (70, 122).

A `subprocess.run` with no `timeout=`, blocked on a network read or an unanswerable prompt,
presents as exactly the reported signature: **0.0% CPU, state `S`, indefinite**.

### Status: hypothesis, NOT confirmed

Per the protocol this is `dynamic` — a claim about what blocks at runtime — so it **cannot** be
confirmed by reading source, and I am not claiming it is. AC1 requires the exact blocking call be
identified by direct observation. No wedged process exists right now to dump.

Two things are in flight:
1. A **py-spy watchdog** is installed at `~/rebar-hang-dumps/watch.sh` (running). It scans once a
   minute for a `rebar review-plan|transition|verify-completion|review-code|sign-review` process
   that has been alive >= 15 min at <= 1% CPU, and on a match writes `py-spy dump`, `py-spy dump
   --locals`, and the process's open TCP/pipe/lock handles to `~/rebar-hang-dumps/hang-<pid>-<ts>.txt`.
   It **captures and does not kill**, so the next occurrence is preserved rather than lost — this
   is what will satisfy AC1.
2. Parallel investigators are tracing the post-model call chain and attempting an experimental
   reproduction of an unbounded block.

### The open discriminator

The hypothesis must still explain observation 1: why did `review-plan` and `transition -> closed`
hang while `comment`, `edit`, `link` and `set-file-impact` completed in seconds, when those also
append to the store and push to the remote? If the blocking call were simply `git push`, the plain
writes should have wedged too. Either the LLM-backed ops reach a call the plain writes never make
(snapshot materialization and attestation signing are the obvious candidates — neither is on the
plain-write path), or the hypothesis is wrong. Not yet resolved, and I am not treating it as
resolved.

compiled_state.description:
## What happened

LLM-backed rebar operations hung **indefinitely** — 0.0% CPU, state `S` (sleeping), no output —
for **3 to 5 hours**, until killed. `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` defaults to 600 s and is wired into both
the Bedrock client (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:95` → `read_timeout`/`connect_timeout`) and a
wall-clock guard (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:376`), so **the configured timeout did not
fire**. This is not "no timeout exists" — it is "the timeout was bypassed or the hang is outside
the region it guards".

## Evidence (observed 2026-08-19/20)

Affected THREE independent sessions in three different worktrees simultaneously, so it is not
workspace-local:

| pid | op | worktree | elapsed | %CPU | state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80532 | `transition … closed` (completion verifier) | noncodebase-tag | 5h00m | 0.0 | S |
| 80534 | `transition … closed` (completion verifier) | noncodebase-tag | 5h00m | 0.0 | S |
| 33196 | `review-plan` | noncodebase-tag | 3h20m | 0.0 | S |
| 31254 | `transition … closed` | impl-obese-dihedral-ermine | 3h41m | 0.0 | S |
| 33211 | `review-plan` | rp05-cli-registry | 3h37m | 0.0 | S |

Discriminating observations:

1. **Only LLM-invoking operations hang.** Every wedged process was `review-plan` or a
   `transition → closed` (which runs the completion verifier). In the same period, non-LLM store
   writes — `rebar session-log append`, `rebar edit`, `rebar comment`, `rebar set-file-impact`,
   `rebar link` — all completed in seconds.
2. **It is NOT store-lock contention.** `lsof .tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` showed **no
   holder** while seven processes were wedged. No per-ticket `.write.lock` existed for the
   affected tickets.
3. **It is NOT slow progress.** 0.0% CPU sustained over hours; a fresh probe run produced
   **zero bytes of output and zero CPU** rather than progressing slowly.
4. **At least one process did LLM work first, then blocked.** pid 33196 (`review-plan`) was
   observed at **87.7% CPU** at t+1h18m and at **0.0% CPU** at t+3h03m — so it completed
   compute and then wedged, which suggests the hang may be AFTER the model call (persisting the
   attestation / a git or network step) rather than in the call itself. This is the main
   ambiguity a root-cause pass must resolve.
5. Killing the wedged processes left every affected ticket cleanly in its prior status with no
   partial event written — the store was not corrupted.

## Why it matters

Every gated operation is affected: no work ticket can be claimed (plan-review gate) or closed
(completion-verification gate) while this is happening. It stalled an entire epic's board
bookkeeping for hours across multiple agent sessions, and the only escape hatch is
`--force=<reason>`, which records **no signed attestation** — i.e. the outage silently degrades
the audit trail if operators work around it.

## Suggested first step

Do NOT assume the model endpoint. The 87.7%→0.0% transition on pid 33196 makes a post-call hang
(attestation write, `git` subprocess, or a second uninstrumented network call) at least as
plausible as a hung provider socket. `/rebar-debug` with a hypothesis-driven pass is the right
protocol; a stack dump (`py-spy dump --pid <pid>`) of a live wedged process would settle it in
one observation, so capture one before killing the next occurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exact blocking call is identified by direct observation (stack dump of a wedged
      process), not inferred.
- [ ] An LLM-backed operation cannot exceed its configured `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` wall clock,
      whatever the blocking layer, and fails with a clear error naming the timed-out stage.
- [ ] A regression test drives the identified blocking layer to hang and asserts the operation
      aborts within the configured budget instead of sleeping indefinitely.
compiled_state.title: LLM-backed rebar ops hang for hours; REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT does not fire
